title: AI For Life
summary: Making practical AI easier to learn, one walkthrough at a time.
problem: New AI users need a clear starting point, understandable terminology, and examples that connect tools to real work.
approach: A student club resource hub brings together tool walkthroughs, business use cases, a searchable glossary, prompts, and a beginner learning roadmap.
demonstrates: Organizing technical information into an approachable learning experience.
limit: An educational resource; tool details need ongoing review as products change.

title: AgencyCRM
summary: A connected workspace for insurance agency operations.
problem: Client records, policies, follow-ups, and appointments can become disconnected across separate tools.
approach: A full-stack application organizes clients, policies, a lead pipeline, tasks, calendars, and reporting around agency workflows.
demonstrates: Turning business workflows into connected interfaces and a relational data model.
limit: Source is private. No public demo or production-readiness claim is presented.

title: Insurance website
summary: A web application for an insurance advisory business.
problem: An advisory business needs an organized digital presence that visitors can navigate and understand.
approach: A React and TypeScript website uses reusable interface components and structured routing.
demonstrates: Building a business-facing web interface with reusable components.
limit: Source is private. A public website address has not been added to this portfolio.

title: AI Apocalypse
summary: An idle simulation about growing an AI startup—and living with the consequences.
problem: An idle game needs progression, meaningful decisions, and a simulation that works independently of its interface.
approach: A TypeScript simulation engine powers a React interface with branching events, progression, and saved games. The project includes automated simulation tests.
demonstrates: Separating game rules from presentation and testing complex state changes.
limit: No public playable build or app-store release is linked here.

title: AI Team
summary: An orchestration workspace for coordinating specialized AI agents.
problem: Multiple AI agents need clear responsibilities, shared task context, and review checkpoints.
approach: A command-driven workspace coordinates agent roles, project tasks, messages, file claims, and review handoffs through terminal sessions.
demonstrates: Designing coordination and review workflows for work across multiple agents.
limit: A development tool, with private source and no public hosted demo.

title: AI Mission Control
summary: A desktop window into an AI team's work.
problem: Managing an agent workspace through terminals alone makes it harder to see activity in one place.
approach: An Electron desktop interface observes the existing orchestration workspace and controls it through its command interface, with terminals and task visibility.
demonstrates: Building a desktop interface around an existing system without duplicating its state.
limit: Requires the underlying local agent workspace; no public download is offered here.

title: Options research lab
summary: A reproducible foundation for studying simulated options execution.
problem: Research results are hard to trust without explicit costs, valid data, and reproducible experiment records.
approach: A Python toolkit validates input data, replays simulated execution, records experiment metadata, and tests accounting and data integrity using synthetic fixtures.
demonstrates: Building auditable research infrastructure and documenting the limits of evidence.
limit: No trading edge has been established. This is offline research, with no live-order code.

title: Mass Email Sender
summary: A desktop workflow for personalized spreadsheet-based email campaigns.
problem: Repeated communication needs personalization, campaign tracking, and a clear review step before sending.
approach: A desktop application organizes templates, spreadsheet imports, business-specific campaigns, previews, and scheduled sends.
demonstrates: Turning a repetitive business process into a guided, reviewable workflow.
limit: A local application; client lists, messages, and account data are not part of this portfolio.

title: Woodworking showcase
summary: A product and storytelling website for handcrafted bookshelves.
problem: A craft business needs a way to explain its story and present its products clearly.
approach: A React website separates editable content from layout, with product, gallery, and story sections.
demonstrates: Structuring a marketing website so content can be maintained in one place.
limit: Business details and photography remain to be completed before launch.
